name: FlashInfer's b12x MoE backend silently defaults quant_mode to W4A4, so a weight-only NVFP4 checkpoint is computed at the wrong activation precision
symptom: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (quant_algo W4A16_NVFP4 for mlp.experts) served with --moe-backend flashinfer_b12x runs the FP4xFP4 micro-kernel (MoEMicroKernel in blackwell_sm12x.moe_micro_kernel, BF16 activations quantized to FP4 in-kernel) instead of the W4A16 kernel in moe_w4a16_kernel.py (FP4 weights dequantized to BF16). The Marlin backend marlin_moe_wna16 does the latter, which is what the checkpoint intends. No error; the kernel runs and returns plausible text at W4A4 precision on a W4A16 checkpoint.
root_cause: A handoff bug across two layers. vLLM's ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.__init__ reads quant_algo W4A16_NVFP4 from hf_quant_config.json, sets self.use_a16 = True, and asks the backend oracle for activation_key=None - but FlashInferB12xExperts._ensure_wrapper() then constructs B12xMoEWrapper with no quant_mode and no activation_precision argument. In flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py the wrapper defaults activation_precision='fp4', quant_mode=None, and _normalize_quant_mode in blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py returns 'w4a16' only if activation_precision == 'bf16' - so it resolves to 'nvfp4'. From there the wrapper allocates nvfp4 workspaces and launch_sm120_moe() skips the 'w4a16' branch. moe_w4a16_kernel.py is never reached because nothing ever asked for it. The class comment's reasoning - 'b12x performs in-kernel BF16->FP4 activation quant, so W4A16 checkpoints are runtime-compatible' - treats W4A16 as 'will not crash', not 'will run at the intended precision'.
workaround: Use the Marlin backend (the reference W4A16 path), or set FLASHINFER_B12X_FORCE_MOE_W4A16=1, which _normalize_quant_mode checks first and which returns 'w4a16' directly. Do not accept a b12x trace showing MoEMicroKernel for a checkpoint whose quant_algo says W4A16.
notes: A silent-precision-loss case with a measured cost: GSM8K accuracy 0.9037 on the correct W4A16 kernel versus 0.9136 for the Marlin reference (1192 vs 1205 correct of the same set), latency 1080 s vs 833 s. The gap is ~1 point, which is exactly the size of quality regression that ships unnoticed and gets attributed to the quantization format rather than to backend selection. Same family of bug as mxfp4-w4a16-misrouted-to-w4a4-kernel - two independent reports of the same class.
